clue.text: State prison reportedly backed by crack troops

indicators.note: backed by puts the next piece behind, after the first
reportedly signals that a word is to be taken by how it is said rather than spelt

parts.note: can is slang for prison
the SAS is the British Army's elite Special Air Service regiment

explanation.surface: A state jail is supported by elite soldiers, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives the spelling KAN for a word that sounds like slang for a jail; 'crack' looks like an adjective of quality but marks elite soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is one of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Produce information, evidence initially seen by judge

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word evidence is used

parts.note: to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A court scene: information and evidence are produced and assessed by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British for information ('the gen on something').
explanation.definitionFit: To produce something is to bring it into being, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fruit tree with bark protected

indicators.note: protected means one piece is wrapped around and shelters the other

parts.note: the maple is a common tree
a yap is a sharp bark of a small dog

explanation.surface: A fruit tree whose bark is shielded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like the tree's covering, which suits 'tree', but it is a dog's noise here.
explanation.definitionFit: The mayapple is a North American woodland plant bearing an edible yellow fruit, also called that fruit's name.

clue.text: Bug is tiny and horrid, ultimately eliminated

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for tiny

indicators.note: ultimately eliminated means the final letter of the word for horrid is dropped

parts.note: vile means horrid

explanation.surface: Someone describing an insect as small and nasty, until it was finally killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately eliminated' removes the last letter, E, from VILE, leaving VIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a kind of beetle, and bug is an everyday word for any insect.

clue.text: Bill's description of the years after 1603?

definitions.meaning: a bill is a printed notice stuck on a wall, a placard
Elizabeth I, ER, died in 1603, so the time following her reign is ...

explanation.surface: Asking how a man called Bill would describe the Jacobean era.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; Elizabeth I died in 1603, so later years are 'post-ER'. 'Bill's' reads as 'Bill is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill in the sense of a printed advertisement pasted up is the same thing as a placard.

clue.text: Work force agreement accepting cuts, oddly

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

indicators.note: accepting means the agreement takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a union is an agreement or alliance

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and other odd-placed letters of the word cuts

explanation.surface: An industrial relations story: workforce agreement accepts job cuts, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives C and T from 'cuts', which go inside UNION after F.
explanation.definitionFit: To function is to work or operate, as a machine does.

clue.text: Stage applause after cricketer finally left field

indicators.note: after means the stage and applause pieces come behind the cricketer pieces

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word left is taken

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or contest
a round of applause, so round means applause

explanation.surface: A cricketer finally leaves the field to a stage-worthy ovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks like a theatre and 'field' a cricket field; both are cricket-flavoured misdirection. 'finally' takes only T from 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleground is a field of battle, as in the field of conflict.

clue.text: Academic going round old university correcting scripts

indicators.note: going round means the academic encloses the other letter

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
Reading is an English university town

explanation.surface: A lecturer goes round an old university marking exam papers.
explanation.walkthrough: READING is a university in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading is checking written text for errors, which is correcting scripts.

clue.text: Worker maybe covering hole over entrance to roadway is engineer

indicators.note: covering means the worker surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a worker bee is one kind of bee, so a worker is an example of a bee

indicators.note: over means the word for hole is read backwards

parts.note: a hole is a mess or predicament, as in being in a hole

indicators.note: entrance to means just the opening letter of the word roadway

explanation.surface: A road worker covers a pothole at a road entrance, and is an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' gives SSEM; 'Worker maybe' is a definition by example. Henry Bessemer invented a Victorian steel-making process.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Bessemer was a Victorian engineer and inventor of a steel-making process.

clue.text: New-born animals eg cats go on this

definitions.meaning: a brood of young animals born together, such as puppies
the granular material in a tray that house cats use as a toilet

explanation.surface: A pet owner's note on kittens and their toilet tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A brood of young born at one birth, and the absorbent stuff in a cat tray, share this one word.

clue.text: Wife once perhaps breaking pickle dish

indicators.note: breaking means one piece splits the other open and sits inside

parts.note: a pickle and a spot are both a tricky situation
an ex is a former spouse, of which a wife once is an example

explanation.surface: A former wife, in a temper, smashes a dish of pickles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' and 'dish' both look like food; one is a fix (SPOT), the other an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for an attractive person, and so is a sexpot.

clue.text: Train mountaineer to avoid cold at great height?

indicators.note: to avoid means the cold letter is left out of the mountaineer

parts.note: a climber is a mountaineer
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
up means high up, aloft

explanation.surface: Advice to a climber training to stay warm at altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid cold' removes C from CLIMBER, leaving LIMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: To limber up is to warm up and exercise before activity, a kind of training.

clue.text: Chivalrous king regularly in the dark?

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards
something done every night after dark happens on a nightly basis

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a gallant monarch is often in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal; here it is part of the phrase for NIGHTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights were bound by a code of chivalry, so gallant conduct is described as befitting a knight.

clue.text: Examiner repelled class almost all of time at school

indicators.note: repelled means the word for class is pushed back, read in reverse

parts.note: a set is a class of pupils grouped by ability

indicators.note: almost all of means the last letter of the school time is lopped off

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year

explanation.surface: An examiner who drove a class away for nearly a whole school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns SET into TES; 'almost all of' cuts TERM to TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is one who tests, which is what an examiner does.

clue.text: A nameless Louisiana native carries round wood

indicators.note: carries means the native holds the next letter inside
nameless means the abbreviation for name, N, is removed

parts.note: a Cajun is a French-descended native of Louisiana
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A Louisiana local with no name carries a log around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N from CAJUN, leaving CAJU, which takes O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Acajou is mahogany, or the wood of the cashew tree, so it is a kind of timber.

clue.text: Who might trounce most boys with intrinsic skill?

definitions.text: Who might trounce most boys with intrinsic skill?

indicators.note: intrinsic means the skill sits within the other letters
to trounce is to beat up, so the letters of most boys are knocked about

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of something

explanation.surface: A clever-clogs child who beats most classmates thanks to natural talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trounce' scrambles the boys' letters into SMYBOOTS, split by 'intrinsic' skill. Read whole, the clue describes the show-off itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart aleck who shows off knowledge is the type who outdoes most boys in class.

clue.text: Pastures new, right, for top performer

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of pastures are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A farmer's fresh fields are just the thing for a champion animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives SUPERSTA; 'Pastures' reads as a farm scene, which hides the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstar is a hugely successful entertainer or sportsperson, a top performer.

clue.text: Happy fool shortly about to appear upset

indicators.note: about means the shortened fool goes around the other piece
shortly means the word for fool is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a gull is someone easily duped, a fool

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to feel can mean to seem or appear, as in it feels right

explanation.surface: A cheerful fool shortly turns out to be distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the fool to GUL; 'upset', in a down clue, reverses the seeming word to LEEF. 'fool shortly' reads as 'fool soon' on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleeful means full of glee, a synonym for happy.

clue.text: Knowingly accepts such a hopeless situation

indicators.note: accepts means the clue word takes the answer within its own letters

explanation.surface: Someone knowingly accepting a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'Knowingly', after the K. 'such a' makes the adjective fit: a no-win situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every outcome is bad, which is hopeless.

clue.text: Ingredient of whisky and port

definitions.meaning: the grain used to make American and Canadian whiskey
a small port town in East Sussex, England, one of the Cinque Ports

explanation.surface: A drinks label listing whisky and port.
explanation.walkthrough: RYE is a historic port town in Sussex; 'port' looks like the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is the cereal distilled into whiskey, and also a Sussex harbour town.

clue.text: Hat put on briefly to cover ears?

indicators.note: to cover means the shortened word wraps around the other piece
briefly means the word for put on loses its last letter

parts.note: clothes are tried on when put on to check the fit
ears of corn are the grain heads of the plant

explanation.surface: A hat worn quickly to keep the ears warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims the put-on word to TRIE; 'ears' suggests the head, but here means heads of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorne is a three-cornered hat of the 18th century.

clue.text: Uninspired philosopher might be so remiss

definitions.meaning: a thinker with no ideas would be lacking in thought

explanation.surface: A thinker with no ideas might be considered negligent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careless and inconsiderate is the same as being remiss, neglectful of others.

clue.text: Cunning cat turning to catch large bird

indicators.note: to catch means the cunning word holds the next letter inside

parts.note: guile is cunning
L is the abbreviation for large in clothing sizes

indicators.note: turning means the word for cat is read backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A crafty cat turns to grab a big bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' gives MOT; 'cat' and 'bird' set a hunting scene that hides the abbreviation for large.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a seabird of the auk family nesting on cliffs.

clue.text: Plant drug-filled cigarette in tycoon's case

indicators.note: in means the cigarette goes inside the casing letters
case means the outer letters of the word tycoon, its casing

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: A joint found in a business magnate's briefcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' gives T and N, the outside of 'tycoon', round REEFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree fern is a large fern with a trunk, a kind of plant.

clue.text: A union leader at front of march, so we hear

indicators.note: at front of places the first pieces before the march
leader means just the opening letter of the word union

parts.note: a rally is a protest march

explanation.surface: A trade union chief at the head of a protest march, so the report goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so we hear' is the definition here, not a signal of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurally means by way of the ears, through hearing.

clue.text: Shilling and foreign coin put together on safe

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the shilling, an old British coin
the ecu was an old French coin
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Coins of two countries put together in a strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin worth twelve pence. 'safe' looks like a strongbox but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure means safe, protected from danger.

clue.text: Mass, composition lacking start of curious vocal piece

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is taken away from the composition

parts.note: an octet is a piece of music for eight instruments

indicators.note: start of means the opening letter of the word curious

explanation.surface: A church Mass whose music has nothing odd about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking start of curious' removes C from OCTET, leaving OTET.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral piece, sung by voices.

clue.text: Fix piano, say

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
say signals an example, as eg does

explanation.surface: Repairing a piano, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To peg something is to fasten or fix it in place.
